column1: # Vendor documentation pages this package cites, and what each one DID when a person read
# it. Checked by `script/check_doc_sources.sh`; see that script's header for why this is
# status-and-destination rather than a content diff, and why a redirect is the signal.
#   url  expect_status  expect_location  observed_on  class  note
# `expect_location` is `-` when the page does not redirect. It is never left blank: TAB is
# IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs collapses into one delimiter and every later column
# `class` is `auto` (a machine can verify this) or `manual` (it cannot — a human must
# re-read it, and the row goes STALE past 180 days to force that).
# Do not edit a row to make the check pass. The row records what someone READ; rewriting
# it to match a fetch nobody looked at turns this file into a rubber stamp.

column6: A dead documentation host this package's history turns on. The host adapter cited this URL; it now 301s to a different site. A 301 is invisible to a browser and to `curl -L` and reads like a rename — here it was the ONLY notice given that Gemini replaced the WebSocket market-data API the price feed ran on. Watched so a change of target, or its removal, is seen.
The index. Gemini proved the index diff is the mechanism that works: the streaming API's removal was announced by absence from this list and by nothing else.

A well-maintained dated changelog going back to 2022-06. Kept for provenance and as a standing negative result: searching four years of it finds `marketdata` 0 times, `l2_updates` 0, `sunset` 0, `breaking` 0. It told us nothing about the one change that mattered.
Machine-readable spec index — the cheapest place a newly added or withdrawn specification shows up.
The REST OpenAPI document `operations-from-specs.txt` was enumerated from.
The AsyncAPI document for the REPLACEMENT websocket API, at a different host from the one this family's feed was built against.

The candles page that lists seven `time_frame` values, three of which the live API rejects, and which contradicts itself (prose `1day`, enum `1d`; only the prose is right). Watched because it is wrong: documentation can be wrong about the thing it exists to specify, and this page is the family's proof.
The replacement streaming API's own page.
The published rate ceilings and the stated burst depth this venue's limiter uses — one of the few venues in the family that documents a burst at all.
Sandbox hosts, which tier-2 tests and `demo-environment.md` depend on.

The streams document `websocket-api-replacement.md` names as its source — the page whose ABSENCE of the old `marketdata` API was the only notice this venue gave that it had replaced the one this family ran on. Unlisted until 2026-09-11, found by this manifest's own coverage check.
One of the four OpenAPI/AsyncAPI documents `endpoint-inventory.md` diffs. The other three were listed and this one was not, which is precisely the kind of gap a manifest nobody audits accumulates.
